title: B1 — Populate `card_concepts`, or formally retire Concept
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B1. Decision recorded in §12 Q2.

## Problem

`card_concepts` exists in the schema (2 FKs + PK) and `seed/index.ts` inserts the 6 `concepts`
rows, but there is **no `cardConcepts` insert anywhere in the codebase** and `CardSeed` has no
`concepts` field. All 6 concepts are therefore orphaned: a Concept node in any view has no edge to
any card.

This is why the v1 `card-argument-taxonomy` view emits no Concept nodes. Emitting them anyway would
require inventing the edges, i.e. authoring ontology inside a projection.

## Interaction

`mechanisms` and `concepts` share slugs on `collectivisation` and `racial-essentialism` — two
tables, two independent `UNIQUE(slug)` constraints, near-duplicate definitions. Populating
`card_concepts` forces a decision on which table owns those two slugs. Per
`docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §9, that collision has been deferred until this issue is addressed.

## Options

1. Populate `card_concepts` from the authored corpus: add a `concepts` field to `CardSeed`, insert
   the link rows with a `relationship` value, resolve the two slug collisions, then add an
   integration test asserting no concept is orphaned.
2. Formally retire Concept: drop the `concepts`/`card_concepts` tables in a migration and remove
   the node type from the view registry.

Option 1 is cheaper and preserves the ontology the ADR already commits to. Option 2 is more honest if
Concept was never actually meant to be used.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q2.
- Every `concepts` row has at least one `card_concepts` row, **or** the tables are dropped.
- The slug collision on `collectivisation` and `racial-essentialism` is resolved, not left ambiguous.
- `verify-seed.ts` covers `card_concepts` so the state is checked by the seed gate.
- The projection view registry is updated accordingly, and the exclusion warning disappears.
- No second ontology is introduced to hold the answer.

title: B2 — Decide the fate of `claim_relations`
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B2. Decision recorded in §12 Q1.

## Problem

`claim_relations` has a full schema — an 11-value `claim_relation_type` enum (SUPPORTS, CHALLENGES,
QUALIFIES, CONTRADICTS, CONTEXTUALISES, EXEMPLIFIES, REQUIRES, GENERALISES, EQUATES,
ANACHRONISTICALLY_MAPS, RETROSPECTIVELY_IDENTIFIES), indexes, and FKs — and **0 rows and no writer**.
No seeder, validator, or test inserts into it.

So the claim↔claim relations named in `ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md` §5 and Issue #3 have no representable
data. The only current carrier of retrospective/anachronistic mapping is
`inference_steps.inference_type`, which is a different proposition: it records how a conclusion was
reached, not that one claim stands in relation to another.

The v1 projection reads `claim_relations` exactly as authored and never infers claim relations from
inference structure. That is correct but means the claim-relation vocabulary is currently
unreachable from the API.

## This is the biggest open ontology question in Issue #3

Deciding this determines whether claim↔claim SUPPORTS / QUALIFIES / ANACHRONISTICALLY_MAPS /
RETROSPECTIVELY_IDENTIFIES edges exist in the domain at all.

## Options

1. Populate `claim_relations` and make it first-class. Author rows for the identity-retrojection
   cluster, where retrospective identification is the actual editorial claim.
2. Retire it as duplicative of the inference-step model, and document that
   `inference_steps.inference_type` is the sole carrier.

Option 1 risks encoding an inference as a relation between two claims — exactly what Q1 forbids the
projection from doing automatically, but which an author could do by hand. Option 2 loses the
vocabulary but removes the ambiguity.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q1.
- Either `claim_relations` has authored rows with an idempotent seeder and a validator, or the
  tables are dropped in a migration and the ADR updated.
- `verify-seed.ts` covers the table so the state is checked by the seed gate.
- If kept: no `claim_relations` row duplicates an `inference_steps` edge. A validator should reject
  a row that merely restates an authored inference.
- If dropped: `docs/ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md` §5 no longer lists claim relations as a vocabulary.
- The projection is unchanged either way — it already reads the table as authored.

title: B4 — Document the deliberate decoupling of status vocabularies
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B4. Decision recorded in §12 Q4.

## Problem

`status` is modelled inconsistently across the ontology:

| Location | Type |
|---|---|
| `cards.epistemic_status`, `claims.epistemic_status` | `epistemic_status` enum |
| `inference_steps.inference_status`, `argument_chains.status` | same-named **`text`**, no vocabulary |
| `evidence_items.evidence_status` | `text`, **no vocabulary at all** |
| `inference_steps.is_canonical` | `boolean` |
| lifecycle | four unrelated enums (`case_status`, `question_status`, `relationship_status`, `contribution_status`) |

So a projection offering one graph-wide status filter or rollup would be unsound. `evidence_status`
in particular has no controlled vocabulary at all — the only part of the ontology where a status is
not even an enum.

## Current mitigation

The v1 projection exposes status **per node type** only and offers no graph-wide status field. The
invariant suite asserts each node carries the status field belonging to its own type and no other.

Per `docs/EVIDENCE_LAYER.md`, "never collapse these" is an explicit documented rule, so decoupling
may well be intentional rather than a defect. That is exactly why this issue is about
**documentation**, not unification.

## This issue decides

Whether the decoupled model is deliberate and should be documented as such, or whether
`inference_steps` / `argument_chains` should migrate onto the `epistemic_status` enum.

Unifying is the wrong move for evidence: epistemic confidence, evidence strength, and lifecycle
progress are genuinely different axes, and collapsing them loses information. But a bare `text`
column with no vocabulary is not defensible either — it can hold any string, including a
misspelling.

## Options

1. Treat the decoupling as intentional. Document it in `ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md`, and give every `text`
   status column an enum or a documented `CHECK` constraint — especially `evidence_status`, which
   currently has no vocabulary whatsoever.
2. Unify `inference_steps` / `argument_chains` onto `epistemic_status`, keeping lifecycle and
   evidence separate.

Option 1 is recommended: it preserves the intentional separation while fixing the real defect, which
is unenforced vocabulary rather than the number of vocabularies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q4.
- Every status column in the schema is either an enum or has a documented vocabulary and a
  constraint that enforces it.
- `evidence_items.evidence_status` in particular gains a documented vocabulary.
- `docs/ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md` states which statuses may be compared and which may not.
- The projection's per-type status contract is unchanged.

title: typecheck:all fails on 8 pre-existing host UI type errors
description:
## Problem

`pnpm run typecheck:all` fails with 8 type errors in the host app. The
Trope Graph work is unaffected — `typecheck:graph` and
`trope-graph:check` are both clean, and the failures predate that work.
Found while wiring the graph into the root tsconfig; recorded in commit
2f31a99 so the green graph check is not mistaken for a green repo.

## Errors

    src/components/ui/resizable.tsx(9,4):   TS2833: Cannot find namespace 'React'. Did you mean 'preact'?
    src/components/ui/resizable.tsx(25,4):  TS2833: Cannot find namespace 'React'. Did you mean 'preact'?
    src/components/ui/skeleton.tsx(6,4):    TS2833: Cannot find namespace 'React'. Did you mean 'preact'?
    src/components/ui/sonner.tsx(4,21):     TS2833: Cannot find namespace 'React'. Did you mean 'preact'?
    src/components/ui/badge.tsx(30,18):     TS2339: Property 'className' does not exist on type 'BadgeProps'
    src/components/ui/sheet.tsx(62,37):     TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to '"bottom" | "left" | "right" | "top"'
    src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx(562,51):  TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"default" | "outline"'
    src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx(562,60):  TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"default" | "sm" | "lg"'

## Root cause: three separate problems

1. **preact `jsxImportSource` vs an absent `React` global.** This is the
   real cause of the 4 TS2833 errors and the reason they cluster. The
   `ui/` components are shadcn components written for React, and they
   use the ambient `React` namespace without importing it:

       // resizable.tsx:9
       }: React.ComponentProps<typeof ResizablePrimitive.PanelGroup>) => (

   That ambient namespace comes from `@types/react`, which is **not
   installed**. `tsconfig.app.json` sets `"jsxImportSource": "preact"`,
   so TS resolves the `React` hint to preact and refuses.

   `package.json` declares both `preact ^10.29.0` and `react ^18.3.1`
   but no `@types/react`, so `react` ships untyped.

2. **`BadgeProps` is missing `className`.** Independent of preact. The
   interface at badge.tsx:26 does not extend a props type that carries
   `className`, yet line 30 destructures it. Compare the sibling
   components, which spread a `React.HTMLAttributes`-style base.

3. **String-to-literal-union narrowing.** Independent of preact. sheet
   and sidebar accept a `string` where cva variants expect a literal
   union, so the value has to be narrowed or typed as the union.

## Notes

- `noImplicitAny`, `strictNullChecks`, and `noUnusedLocals` are all off in
  the root tsconfig, so this is not a strictness migration. It is three
  genuine type errors.
- Deciding between "install @types/react" and "rewrite these components
  against preact" is a project-level call about which React surface is
  authoritative. Worth settling deliberately rather than installing
  @types/react reflexively — preact and React types are not drop-in
  equivalent, and adding @types/react may surface further errors.

title: B5 — Resolve the competing claim→source attachment paths
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B5. Decision recorded in §12 Q4.
Blocks the `evidence` view only; not a v1 blocker (0 rows today).

## Problem

A source can be attached to a claim through **four** different tables:

- `claim_sources` — claim→source directly, with `quote_or_excerpt` and `page_reference`
- `interpretation_sources` — interpretation→source
- `question_sources` — question→source
- `evidence_sources` — evidence→source

`claim_sources` bypasses the located-passage model entirely: it records that a source backs a claim
without recording *where* in the source the support is. `docs/EVIDENCE_LAYER.md` explicitly says
do not use `claim_sources` when the passage is known — but the table remains, is nullable-relationship
varied, and has `relationship NOT NULL` while three sibling columns are nullable.

The `evidence` view therefore has no unambiguous claim→source path. The projection cannot decide
which of two populated paths is authoritative.

## Why it is not a v1 blocker

`sources`, all five `evidence_*` tables, and `claim_sources` have 0 rows. The v1
`card-argument-taxonomy` view emits no Source or Evidence node, so the ambiguity is not yet
reachable. It becomes a blocker the moment the evidence corpus is populated.

## Options

1. Deprecate `claim_sources`: when a passage is known, use the evidence model. Keep the table for
   genuinely passage-less attachments, and document that rule.
2. Retire `claim_sources` outright and require all claim→source support to go through evidence.

Option 1 is safer for the existing corpus, which has no evidence rows at all, so a hard retirement
would have no replacement path.

## Also fold in

The eight "how are these related" columns (`claim_sources.relationship`, `interpretation_sources.relationship`,
`card_concepts.relationship`, plus four evidence `relation` columns) have differing nullability and
defaults and no shared vocabulary. Whichever option is chosen should reconcile them.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q4 and in `docs/EVIDENCE_LAYER.md`.
- `claim_sources` is either dropped or carries a documented rule for when it may be used.
- The `relationship` columns have a shared, enforced vocabulary, or are consolidated.
- The `evidence` view can resolve claim→source unambiguously, with a test asserting it.

B3 — Harden `relationships` referential integrity
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B3. Decision recorded in §12 Q5.

## Problem

`relationships` is polymorphic with no referential integrity:

- `from_entity_type` / `to_entity_type` are free `text`, not an enum.
- `from_entity_id` / `to_entity_id` are plain uuids with **no foreign keys**.

A reader cannot verify that an endpoint exists, nor that a `*_entity_type` string names a real type.
All 11 live rows happen to be `CARD→CARD`, so the table is safe today and unsafe the moment someone
inserts `CLAIM→CONCEPT` or a stale uuid.

## Current mitigation (in the v1 projection)

A `relationships` row becomes an edge **only** when both discriminators are exactly `CARD` and both
uuids resolve to cards. Anything else is dropped and recorded in `meta.warnings[]`. Edges are
additionally re-checked against the emitted node set after traversal, so a relationship to a card
beyond the traversal frontier cannot produce a dangling edge. Integration tests assert this over all
47 seeded cards.

This is deliberately a *reader-side* mitigation. It makes the projection safe without changing the
schema, per the Issue #3 constraint not to modify the database schema. The schema defect remains.

## Options

1. Replace the polymorphic pair with typed FK columns per entity pair (many columns, strong
   integrity, awkward to extend).
2. Introduce an `entity_type` enum for the discriminators and keep the uuids unconstrained.
3. Keep polymorphic, and accept the defensive projection filter as permanent.

Option 1 is the only one that can actually prevent a dangling edge at write time.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q5.
- If hardened: no `relationships` row can be inserted whose endpoints do not exist, enforced by the
  database rather than by application code.
- `from_entity_type` / `to_entity_type` are constrained to known types.
- If option 3 is chosen: the projection's defensive filter stays, is tested, and the trade-off is
  documented in `docs/ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md`.
- Any orphaned rows are removed or repaired by a migration, and `verify-seed.ts` covers the table.
